text:
The best thing happening in San Jose right now has three young names on it. Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg combined for eight points in a 4-2 win over Nashville, and San Jose Hockey Now's headline put it simply: "Kids Are Alright." Smith had a goal and two assists, and the Sharks have won three of four.

Smith, 21, has 18 points in 23 games at 19:47 a night, and his goals (8) sit right on his chances (9.0 expected). His talent range says there's more coming: 0.96 expected goals per 60 last season, 1.19 now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the league's best at getting to the slot (98th percentile) and at taking shots off passes across it.

The worry is the other end. San Jose gets only 46.6% of the expected goals with him at five on five, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating more against him last season than against all but 8% of forwards. What to watch: whether the new line holds, and whether he gets his own power play unit, as Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest argued after the second unit scored twice without him driving it.
headline: Will Smith and the Sharks' kid line
